lines.line: Watch a river. It never stops, day or night. Neither does your time.
And while we keep saying 'later', life speeds right past us.
lines.credit: Seneca · Letters to Lucilius 1, tr. Gummere

lines.line: Too late? Midlife starters had nearly the same low death risk as lifelong movers.
lines.credit: Saint-Maurice et al. · JAMA Netw Open, 2019

lines.line: So move tomorrow's job to today, and today's job to right now.
Then shoot like you have one arrow. No second try. This one counts.
A cellist of 81 practised hours daily. Why? He felt he was still improving.
And yoga asks for balance: food, sleep, work, never too much or too little.
Can you get down to the floor and up easily? That predicted longer life.
lines.credit: L. B. Brito et al. · Eur J Prev Cardiol, 2014

lines.line: Not just longer. Real life is living in good health.
So, to all who practise: don't let your time flow past unused. Practise today.
Our life is a dewdrop on the grass. The sun is already rising.
No day gets a second morning. Use this one: the years won't wait.
Looking back, no one regretted learning a skill. The biggest regrets: things never done.
lines.credit: Gilovich & Medvec · J Pers Soc Psychol, 1994

lines.line: Hard to get up? Remember: you rise to do a human being's work.
lines.credit: Marcus Aurelius · Meditations V.1, tr. Long

lines.line: Then treat this morning's practice as a meeting that comes once in a lifetime.
Mornings start the night before. Basketball players who slept more ran faster, shot better.
lines.credit: C. D. Mah et al. · Sleep, 2011

lines.line: Add the basics: moderate exercise, and just enough food to refuel, not overload.
lines.credit: Cicero · On Old Age, tr. Falconer

lines.line: At 107, she had just released her sixth piano album. 'Youth is inside us.'
While your body is well, put your biggest effort into what matters most.
For 80 years, Casals began each day playing Bach. Begin yours: practise today.
His Olympic marathon took over 54 years. Meanwhile, he married and had six children.
After 30, muscle slowly fades. Training and good food can change that a lot.
lines.credit: E. Volpi et al. · Curr Opin Clin Nutr, 2004

lines.line: A nun began training at 48. At 82, she crossed an Ironman finish line.
No time? Five to ten minutes of slow running daily went with longer life.
lines.credit: D. C. Lee et al. · J Am Coll Cardiol, 2014

lines.line: Small or big, whatever task you find, give it all your strength.
And yoga itself means skill in action: doing each task well.
At 105 he sprinted 100 metres in Kyoto. His secret: health comes first.
And health starts at the table: stop eating at about 80% full.
Lifelong skiers aged 80 and over had fitness like ordinary men 40 years younger.
lines.credit: S. Trappe et al. · J Appl Physiol, 2013

lines.line: One day of full effort is better than a hundred lazy years. Practise today.
lines.credit: The Buddha · Dhammapada 112, tr. Max Müller

lines.line: An inch of time is an inch of gold. You're spending some now.
Yet we keep saying 'tomorrow.' Thai calls it: put off the day, promise tomorrow.
lines.credit: ผัดวันประกันพรุ่ง · Thai idiom

lines.line: Yesterday is gone. Tomorrow hasn't come. Today is the day to work hard.
lines.credit: The Buddha · Majjhima Nikaya 131, tr. Sujato

lines.line: Still dancing at 100, she heard 'I wish I could.' Her answer: do it.
But our minds wander almost half the time, which is linked to less happiness.
The fix: give each thing your whole mind. On the mat, only the mat.
Health comes first. It is the root of goodness, wealth, joy and inner freedom.
Exercise like brisk walking, up to 75 minutes weekly, went with 1.8 more years.
lines.credit: S. C. Moore et al. · PLoS Medicine, 2012

lines.line: Long life brings joy: each day you learn, each month you can do more.
Now is the only time you can use. So spend it on the mat.
